answer: New identities enter on a marble pass that stays inert until the holder answers a series of unannounced onyx roll-calls spread across a long horizon. Each call demands, within seconds, a fresh proof tied to that identity's own past work, so one operator running n clones must be live for all of them at once. Overlapping calls force parallel attention and separate computation per clone, so total cost grows faster than n, and a missed call resets the pass — clones cannot share one operator's presence.
